reason: keys is a set used only for its key set: the next statements range over it (`for gk := range keys`) and never read a value, so a block is in the set whether the stored value is true or false.

h.joined is a set. Its value is read once, in `dup || h.joined[r.Item]`, to skip a second listing of an item this call already joined; with false that second listing falls through to the in-flight check, finds the same in-flight entry and assigns the same entry again, which is the same outcome. Every other use ranges over the keys (holders++ at reservation, release at the end), and the key is present whatever the value.
